newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Belarus leader warns OSCE not to interfere.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader warns OSCE not to interfere.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, responding to criticism at a European security summit, defended his country's record on democracy on Monday and warned other countries not to interfere.

"It would be counterproductive to try to exert pressure on us or try to interfere in our internal affairs," Lukshenko told the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) meeting in Lisbon.
"We expect from the OSCE the corresponding attitude and compliance with the existing rules and procedures governing its relations with states participating in the organisation," Lukashenko said.
Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, chairman in office of the OSCE, had told the opening session of the summit that he was "deeply concerned" by developments in Belarus.

But Lukashenko defended the much-criticised referendum on November 24 in which he won backing for strengthening his powers in the former Soviet republic. He said Belarus, a country of 10 million people, had solved its problems democraticlly.

Lukashenko specifically mentioned the United States in his attack, following Washington's criticism of his autocratic rule. He also opposed NATO's plans to expand eastwards up to Belarus's border, saying this could create a new "schism" in Europe.
